title: The Information-Processing Model: Encoding, Storage & Retrieval
description: Understand sensory memory, Baddeley's working memory model, explicit vs implicit LTM, and levels of processing.

slides.title: The Three-Stage Memory Architecture 💾
slides.content:
# The Atkinson-Shiffrin Model

Human memory functions as an information-processing system with three primary stages:

1. **Sensory Memory**: High-capacity, fleeting buffer capturing raw sensory input.
   * **Iconic Memory**: Visual sensory register lasting ~0.25 to 0.5 seconds (demonstrated by George Sperling's partial-report technique).
   * **Echoic Memory**: Auditory sensory register lasting 3 to 4 seconds.
2. **Short-Term / Working Memory**: Active, conscious workspace.
   * Capacity: George Miller's classic **7 ± 2 items** (modern estimates suggest 4 ± 1 chunks).
   * Duration: ~15 to 30 seconds without active rehearsal.
3. **Long-Term Memory (LTM)**: Relatively permanent and virtually limitless storehouse of knowledge and experience.

quizData.question: What is the brief sensory memory for auditory sounds that lingers for approximately 3 to 4 seconds called?
quizData.explanation: Echoic memory is the fleeting auditory sensory register that holds acoustic traces for several seconds.

slides.title: Subtypes of Long-Term Memory 🗄️
slides.content:
## Explicit vs. Implicit Systems | Category | Subtype | Neural Substrate | Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Explicit (Declarative)**
*Conscious recollection* | **Episodic Memory** | Hippocampus & Prefrontal Cortex | Recalling your high school graduation day | | | **Semantic Memory** | Temporal Lobes & Association Cortex | Knowing that Paris is the capital of France | | **Implicit (Nondeclarative)**
*Without conscious recall* | **Procedural Memory** | Cerebellum & Basal Ganglia | Knowing how to balance and pedal a bicycle | | | **Classical Conditioning & Priming** | Amygdala, Cerebellum & Sensory Cortex | Salivating at the chime of an ice cream truck |

slides.title: Encoding: Levels of Processing 🔬
slides.content:
## Craik & Lockhart's Paradigm

How well you remember information depends on the **depth of cognitive processing** during encoding:

* **Shallow Processing**: Structural encoding (noticing visual font, CAPITAL vs lowercase) or Phonemic encoding (rhyming words). Produces weak, transient memories.
* **Deep (Semantic) Processing**: Analyzing the actual meaning and conceptual relationships of the material.
* **Self-Reference Effect**: Information deemed personally relevant and related to oneself is remembered far more vividly than generic information!

quizData.question: Your ability to seamlessly type on a keyboard or tie your shoes without consciously thinking through each movement is stored in which memory system?
quizData.explanation: Procedural memory governs motor skills and physical actions that operate implicitly without deliberate conscious retrieval.

slides.title: The Testing Effect (Retrieval Practice) 💡
slides.content:
## Active Recall Beats Passive Re-reading

Cognitive research consistently shows that **active retrieval practice** (flashcards, practice quizzes) strengthens neural memory traces far more effectively than spending equal time re-reading textbook passages. Struggle during retrieval signals the brain that the memory is high priority!
